finding.claim: Blind SSRF: user-supplied callbackUrl is stored with no validation and later POSTed to by the server every minute. An attacker can target internal hosts, localhost or cloud metadata endpoints (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/), and the payload is sent as the POST body. The response is discarded, so the SSRF is blind. The scheme is unrestricted, though java.net.http supports only http and https.
finding.source: callbackUrl parameter of POST /subscribe, supplied by any caller (Jobs.java:12-13)
finding.sink: HttpClient.send with HttpRequest built from URI.create(cb) (Jobs.java:20-24)

trace.note: subscribe(name, callbackUrl) receives the attacker-controlled URL
URL stored unvalidated in the static subscriptions map
notifyAll iterates over the stored callback URLs
URI.create(cb) builds the request URI with no host or scheme checks
client.send issues the request from the server network position

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host or allowlist check, and no private, loopback or link-local IP blocking. Nothing is resolved or re-checked at send time, so DNS rebinding also works. There is no authentication visible in this file. HttpClient.newHttpClient() does not follow redirects by default, but that does not mitigate the direct request.

verdict.reason: src/Jobs.java:13-14 stores callbackUrl unvalidated and src/Jobs.java:19-24 POSTs to URI.create(cb) with no scheme, host or IP checks (the only regex guard, at line 30, protects thumb() and not this path), so the blind SSRF holds.
